# Environment

```{r fig.height=13, fig.width=6, dpi=300}
# --- 1) Build a 1° sf grid and aggregate env fields into it -------------------

# Points -> sf (keep lon/lat in data for reference if helpful)
pts_env <- st_as_sf(env_df, coords = c("lon360", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# Make a global-ish 1° grid over the points' extent
grid_1deg <- st_make_grid(pts_env, cellsize = c(1,1), what = "polygons", square = TRUE)
grid_1deg <- st_sf(cell_id = seq_along(grid_1deg), geometry = grid_1deg)

# Spatial join points to grid cells, then summarize by cell (mean of each temp)
grid_env <- st_join(grid_1deg, pts_env, join = st_intersects, left = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(cell_id) |>
  summarise(
    Tp = mean(Tp, na.rm = TRUE),
    Tm = mean(Tm, na.rm = TRUE),
    Tb = mean(Tb, na.rm = TRUE),
    pO2p = mean(pO2p, na.rm = TRUE),
    pO2m = mean(pO2m, na.rm = TRUE),
    pO2b = mean(pO2b, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  right_join(grid_1deg, by = "cell_id") |>
  st_as_sf()

# Land layer
world <- ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf")

# 
sym_lims <- function(x) {
  L <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  U <- max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  c(L, U)
}

# ---- replace your map_panel() with a diverging version ----
map_panel_diverging <- function(data, var, title, legend_title, limits, colors) {
  ggplot(data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = .data[[var]]), color = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = world, fill = "black", color = "black") +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low       = colors[1],      # negative end (keep your existing extreme)
      high       = colors[2],        # 0 is white
      limits    = limits, 
      oob       = scales::squish, # clamp out-of-range to ends
      na.value  = "transparent",
      name      = legend_title,
      guide     = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        barwidth       = unit(10, "cm"),
        barheight      = unit(0.4, "cm")
      )
    ) +
    coord_sf(crs = "+proj=moll", expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      plot.background  = element_blank(),
      axis.text        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
      axis.title       = element_blank(),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.title       = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5)
    )
}

# ---- Temperature panels (shared symmetric limits) ----
lims_Tp <- sym_lims(c(grid_env$Tp))
lims_Tm <- sym_lims(c(grid_env$Tm))
lims_Tb <- sym_lims(c(grid_env$Tb))

p_Tp <- map_panel_diverging(
  grid_env, "Tp",
  title = "Pelagic temperature (°C)",
```

```{r fig.height=10, fig.width=6, dpi=300}
# --- Helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

# classify into {- , 0 , +} with an optional zero tolerance band (in data units)
classify_sign <- function(x, zero_tol = 0){
  cls <- dplyr::case_when(
    x >  zero_tol            ~ "positive",
    x < -zero_tol            ~ "negative",
    is.finite(x)             ~ "zero",
    TRUE                     ~ NA_character_
  )
  factor(cls, levels = c("negative","zero","positive"))
}

# three-color panel (Mollweide), using the sign classes
map_panel_three <- function(data, var, title, legend_title, zero_tol = 0){
  df_plot <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sign_class = classify_sign(.data[[var]], zero_tol))

  ggplot(df_plot) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = sign_class), color = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = world, fill = "black", color = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(negative = "#D3D694", zero = "white", positive = "#674776"),
      drop = FALSE,
      name = legend_title,
      labels = c("Decrease (<0)", "No change (~0)", "Increase (>0)")
    ) +
    coord_sf(crs = "+proj=moll", expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      plot.background  = element_blank(),
      axis.text        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
      axis.title       = element_blank(),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.title       = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5)
    )
}


# e.g., treat |ΔpO2| < 0.05 kPa as "zero"
z_tol <- 0.5

p_pO2p_sign <- map_panel_three(
  grid_env, "pO2p",
  title = "Pelagic oxygen change (sign)",
  legend_title = expression(Delta*pO[2]*" sign"),
  zero_tol = z_tol
)

p_pO2b_sign <- map_panel_three(
  grid_env, "pO2b",
  title = "Bottom oxygen change (sign)",
  legend_title = expression(Delta*pO[2]*" sign"),
  zero_tol = z_tol
)

p_pO2p_sign / p_pO2b_sign
```

```{r}
# 1) Area weights (1° grid): proportional to cos(latitude)
env_w <- env_df %>%
  mutate(weight = pmax(0, cos(pi * lat / 180)))  # guard against tiny negatives at poles

# 2) Shared bin edges across all depths so panels are directly comparable
T_all   <- c(env_w$Tp, env_w$Tm, env_w$Tb)
O2_all  <- c(env_w$pO2p, env_w$pO2m, env_w$pO2b)

T_range <- range(T_all,  na.rm = TRUE)
O2_range <- range(O2_all, na.rm = TRUE)

# Choose sensible bin widths; tweak as you like
dT  <- 1.0
dO2 <- 1.0
T_breaks  <- seq(floor(T_range[1]), ceiling(T_range[2]), by = dT)
O2_breaks <- seq(floor(O2_range[1]), ceiling(O2_range[2]), by = dO2)

# Helper to make a weighted T–pO2 surface for one depth
make_surface <- function(df, T_col, O2_col, depth_label, T_breaks, O2_breaks) {
  T_sym  <- rlang::ensym(T_col)
  O2_sym <- rlang::ensym(O2_col)

  bin_center <- function(brks) head(brks, -1) + diff(brks) / 2

  dat <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!T_sym), !is.na(!!O2_sym), weight > 0) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      T_bin  = cut(!!T_sym,  breaks = T_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE),
      O2_bin = cut(!!O2_sym, breaks = O2_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
    )

  denom <- sum(dat$weight, na.rm = TRUE)

  surf <- dat %>%
    dplyr::group_by(T_bin, O2_bin) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(wsum = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::complete(T_bin, O2_bin, fill = list(wsum = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      pct     = 100 * wsum / denom,
      pct_plot = ifelse(pct <= 0, NA_real_, pct),     # <= 0 becomes transparent
      depth   = depth_label,
      T_mid   = bin_center(T_breaks)[as.integer(T_bin)],
      O2_mid  = bin_center(O2_breaks)[as.integer(O2_bin)]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(depth, T_mid, O2_mid, pct, pct_plot)

  return(surf)
}

# 3) Build surfaces for each depth
surf_p <- make_surface(env_w, "Tp", "pO2p", "Pelagic",  T_breaks, O2_breaks)
surf_m <- make_surface(env_w, "Tm", "pO2m", "Midwater", T_breaks, O2_breaks)
surf_b <- make_surface(env_w, "Tb", "pO2b", "Bottom",   T_breaks, O2_breaks)

# Limits based on positive coverage only

p_cov <- ggplot(surf_all, aes(x = T_mid, y = O2_mid, fill = pct_plot)) +
  geom_tile(color = NA) +
```

```{r}
#--------------------------
# 0) Helpers
#--------------------------

# Parse depth columns like "X0","X5","X375" -> numeric meters
to_long_depth <- function(df, value_name) {
  depth_cols <- grep("^X\\d+$", names(df), value = TRUE)
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, dplyr::all_of(depth_cols)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols      = dplyr::all_of(depth_cols),
      names_to  = "depth_str",
      values_to = value_name
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(depth_m = as.numeric(sub("^X", "", depth_str))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-depth_str)
}

# Infer global grid spacing (median Δlat, Δlon in degrees)
infer_grid_spacing <- function(lat_vec, lon_vec) {
  dlat <- lat_vec %>% unique() %>% sort() %>% diff() %>% abs()
  dlon <- lon_vec %>% unique() %>% sort() %>% diff() %>% abs()
  tibble::tibble(
    dlat = stats::median(dlat, na.rm = TRUE),
    dlon = stats::median(dlon, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Cell area (m^2) at latitude for a lat-lon cell of size dlat × dlon (degrees)
cell_area_m2 <- function(lat_deg, dlat_deg, dlon_deg) {
  R <- 6371000
  lat  <- lat_deg  * pi/180
  dlat <- dlat_deg * pi/180
  dlon <- dlon_deg * pi/180
  (R^2) * abs(sin(lat + dlat/2) - sin(lat - dlat/2)) * dlon
}

# Compute layer top/bottom and thickness at each sample depth (per location)
# Uses half-gap to neighbors; topmost extends to 0 m; bottommost extends by half of upper gap
# If only one depth exists, uses default_half_thickness_m on both sides.
add_layer_thickness <- function(df_loc, default_half_thickness_m = 50) {
  df_loc <- df_loc %>% dplyr::arrange(depth_m)

  gap_up   <- df_loc$depth_m - dplyr::lag(df_loc$depth_m)
  gap_down <- dplyr::lead(df_loc$depth_m) - df_loc$depth_m

  top    <- ifelse(is.na(gap_up),
                   0,
                   df_loc$depth_m - gap_up/2)
  bottom <- ifelse(is.na(gap_down),
                   df_loc$depth_m + ifelse(is.na(gap_up), default_half_thickness_m, gap_up/2),
                   df_loc$depth_m + gap_down/2)

  df_loc$layer_top_m    <- top
  df_loc$layer_bottom_m <- bottom
  df_loc$layer_thick_m  <- pmax(0, bottom - top)
  df_loc
}

# Overlap of a layer with a regime [zmin, zmax] (meters; positive down)
overlap_thickness <- function(layer_top, layer_bottom, zmin, zmax) {
  pmax(0, pmin(layer_bottom, zmax) - pmax(layer_top, zmin))
}

# Bin edges (shared across depths/regimes)
make_breaks <- function(x, binwidth = NULL, n = 40) {
  rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(binwidth)) {
    pretty(rng, n = n)
  } else {
    seq(floor(rng[1]/binwidth)*binwidth, ceiling(rng[2]/binwidth)*binwidth, by = binwidth)
  }
}

# 2D binning into sum(volume) with zeros kept; returns bin centers for plotting
bin_volume_2d <- function(df, T_col, O2_col, vol_col, T_breaks, O2_breaks, depth_label) {
  T_sym  <- rlang::ensym(T_col)
  O2_sym <- rlang::ensym(O2_col)
  V_sym  <- rlang::ensym(vol_col)

  # function for centers
  bin_center <- function(brks) head(brks, -1) + diff(brks)/2

  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!T_sym), !is.na(!!O2_sym), !is.na(!!V_sym), !!V_sym > 0) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      T_bin  = cut(!!T_sym,  breaks = T_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE),
      O2_bin = cut(!!O2_sym, breaks = O2_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(T_bin, O2_bin) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(volume_m3 = sum(!!V_sym, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::complete(T_bin, O2_bin, fill = list(volume_m3 = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      T_mid  = bin_center(T_breaks)[as.integer(T_bin)],
      O2_mid = bin_center(O2_breaks)[as.integer(O2_bin)],
      depth  = depth_label,
      volume_km3 = volume_m3 / 1e9  # optional unit for nicer legend
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(depth, T_mid, O2_mid, volume_m3, volume_km3)
}

#--------------------------
# 1) Prepare long-form data and areas
#--------------------------

T_long  <- to_long_depth(T_df,   "T")
O2_long <- to_long_depth(pO2_df, "pO2")

# Keep only rows where at least one of T or pO2 is present; we’ll filter per regime later
df_long <- dplyr::full_join(
  T_long, O2_long,
  by = c("LATITUDE","LONGITUDE","depth_m")
)

# Infer spacing and compute cell area per (lat, lon)
sp <- infer_grid_spacing(df_long$LATITUDE, df_long$LONGITUDE)
df_long <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cell_area_m2 = cell_area_m2(LATITUDE, sp$dlat, sp$dlon))

# Assign layer thickness per (lat, lon)
df_long <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ add_layer_thickness(.x)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

#--------------------------
# 2) Regime-specific volumes
#--------------------------

# Pelagic: 0–100 m
pelagic <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    overlap_m = overlap_thickness(layer_top_m, layer_bottom_m, 0, 100),
    vol_m3    = cell_area_m2 * overlap_m
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(overlap_m > 0, !is.na(T), !is.na(pO2))

# Midwater: 500–1500 m (skip rows without those depths by overlap=0)
midwater <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    overlap_m = overlap_thickness(layer_top_m, layer_bottom_m, 500, 1500),
    vol_m3    = cell_area_m2 * overlap_m
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(overlap_m > 0, !is.na(T), !is.na(pO2))

# Bottom: deepest non-NA T & pO2 per location
bottom_candidates <- df_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(T), !is.na(pO2)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(depth_m == max(depth_m, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

bottom <- bottom_candidates %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # use full layer thickness around that deepest sample
    overlap_m = pmax(0, layer_thick_m),
    vol_m3    = cell_area_m2 * overlap_m
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(overlap_m > 0)
```


```{r}
#--------------------------
# 3) Shared bins and 2D volume histograms
#--------------------------
T_all   <- c(pelagic$T, midwater$T, bottom$T)
O2_all  <- c(pelagic$pO2, midwater$pO2, bottom$pO2)

T_breaks  <- make_breaks(T_all,  binwidth = 0.5)   # 1 °C bins (tune as needed)
O2_breaks <- make_breaks(O2_all, binwidth = 0.5)   # 1 kPa bins (tune as needed)

surf_p <- bin_volume_2d(pelagic, "T", "pO2", "vol_m3", T_breaks, O2_breaks, "Pelagic (0–100 m)")
surf_m <- bin_volume_2d(midwater, "T", "pO2", "vol_m3", T_breaks, O2_breaks, "Midwater (500–1500 m)")
surf_b <- bin_volume_2d(bottom,   "T", "pO2", "vol_m3", T_breaks, O2_breaks, "Bottom (deepest sampled)")

surf_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(surf_p, surf_m, surf_b)

# Optional: drop true zeros so they plot "clear"
surf_all <- surf_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(volume_km3_plot = dplyr::if_else(volume_km3 <= 0, NA_real_, volume_km3))

depth_order <- c("Pelagic (0–100 m)", "Midwater (500–1500 m)", "Bottom (deepest sampled)")

surf_all <- surf_all %>% dplyr::mutate(depth = factor(depth, levels = depth_order))

panel_plot <- function(df, title, fill_var = "volume_km3_plot", legend_title = "Ocean volume (km³)") {
  ggplot(df, aes(T_mid, O2_mid, fill = .data[[fill_var]])) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis(option = "viridis", name = legend_title, na.value = "transparent") +
    labs(title = title, x = "Temperature (°C)", y = expression(paste("pO"[2], " (kPa)"))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      legend.title     = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
}

pvol_1 <- panel_plot(dplyr::filter(surf_all, depth == depth_order[1]), "Pelagic")
pvol_2 <- panel_plot(dplyr::filter(surf_all, depth == depth_order[2]), "Midwater") +
      theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())  # tidy center panel
pvol_3 <- panel_plot(dplyr::filter(surf_all, depth == depth_order[3]), "Bottom") +
      theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())

pvol_1 + pvol_2 + pvol_3
```
